text:
Ibrahim Noor: Hey all, first-day setup question. Running local compose (web + postgres + redis) on Mac M1. Postgres container starts but my app on host can't connect. I also put init SQLs in ./db/init but they didn't apply. Docker logs show "skipping initialization". Anyone have a quick checklist?

Sofia Alvarez: Welcome! Quick checklist: 1) Are you mapping a host dir to Postgres data? If so the entrypoint only runs init on an empty PGDATA dir. 2) Check PGDATA env and where you mount the volume: if PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata but you mount ./pgdata to /var/lib/postgresql/data, postgres may see existing files and skip init. 3) For host apps on mac use host.docker.internal or publish the port (e.g., "15432:5432") to avoid homebrew postgres conflicts.

Ibrahim Noor: I did set PGDATA in compose to /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata and mounted to /var/lib/postgresql/data. That explains it. How should I safely force re-init?

Sofia Alvarez: If you don't need the data, `docker-compose down -v` then remove the named volume or host dir (e.g., `rm -rf ./pgdata/*`). If using a named volume, find it with `docker volume ls` and `docker volume rm <name>`. For safety, back up anything you need first. Also ensure init files are readable (chmod 644).

infra-bot: Dev docs: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup has Mac M1 tips, recommended compose snippets, and a .env.local.template.

Ibrahim Noor: Thanks — switching mount to match PGDATA, nuking the volume, and will re-run. If I keep running the app on host I'll map to 15432. Appreciate the help!
